items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

ctx.x: Columbia Record Club. So I got my record for the month and I got my Don Ellis. It was like 7:30 in the morning. I put it on — all this drumming and all this odd meters. And I was like whoa my God. And I was like a 15, 16 year old. And that really hit me. And I wore out that album, I loved it. So yeah, that’s one of the ones that, it really changed my life because it wanted me to have something and it made me feel good when I heard that album. Yes. And seeing the Stan Kenton band back in 1967 or so, I was only…

Yeah, it’s easy to sound like these aren’t the good old days. We had the good old days. But I think the process of going to a record store and hearing something on the radio and seeking it out and buying a physical product, at least for our generation, worked for us.
